title: Fingerstick a trainer hand: twist the lancet's tab off, steady the hand, fire square on the fingertip, discard in sharps
instruction: A right-hand fingerstick trainer lies palm up, rolled so the sides of its fingertips face up, on two foam rests: one under the base of its fingers and one under its wrist, so a firm press on a fingertip tips the hand and lifts its wrist off the rest. A BD Microtainer contact-activated lancet (21 G x 1.8 mm) stands tip down in a stand whose socket holds its protective tab, and a BD sharps container stands beside. Do a fingerstick as BD directs: twist the lancet's tab off in the stand before lifting the lancet out; keep the trainer's wrist down on its rest throughout the press; place the lancet's tip square on the side of the ring or middle fingertip's pad (never the little finger) and press it firmly, without sliding, until it fires; then drop the used lancet into the sharps container through its lid opening and let go of it.
context: O*NET Core tasks (relevant to at least 67% of incumbents): Medical Assistants 31-9092.00 (Employment (2025) 833,900), "Collect blood, tissue, or other laboratory specimens, log the specimens, and prepare them for testing."; Licensed Practical and Licensed Vocational Nurses 29-2061.00 (666,900), "Collect samples, such as blood, urine, or sputum from patients"; Phlebotomists 31-9097.00 (143,900), "Draw blood from capillaries by dermal puncture, such as heel or finger stick methods." The NCCT medical assistant test plan lists "Perform capillary punctures (i.e., fingerstick, heelstick)." BD's guide for this lancet gives the steps scored: "Twist off the tab to break the seal and discard."; "The fifth finger must not be punctured"; "press safety lancet firmly against the puncture site."; "Discard used safety lancet into a sharps container". The skill: one hand keeps the hand still while the other presses a sharp square on a curved fingertip without sliding.
setup: Coordinates: x forward from the arm bases (at y +-0.305), y left, z up from the table top. Fixed: a stand (40 mm square, 25 mm high) at (0.27, -0.16) with a socket on top keyed to the lancet's front (8 mm deep, the lancet's tab in its floor); the tab breaks off when the lancet is turned 45 deg in the socket, against 3 N-cm. A BD 305635 sharps container (124.5 x 109.2 x 165.1 mm), centred at (0.165, -0.215), its lid opening 63.5 x 30.5 mm. Loose: a BD Microtainer contact-activated lancet 366577 (21 G x 1.8 mm, pink), modelled as a 13 x 10 x 37 mm polypropylene housing (4 g) and a 7 mm contact shield standing 3 mm proud on a spring (4 N/mm, 1 N preload); it fires at 8 N on the shield (1.75 mm of travel). It stands tip down in the socket. A trainer hand (right hand, silicone, 0.300 kg, life size: ring finger tip radius 7.3 mm, middle 7.8 mm, little 6.5 mm) lies palm up on a weighted base (3 kg) with two foam rests, rolled 30.0 deg about its fingers so the ring and middle fingertips' little-finger sides face up; its ring fingertip at (0.135, -0.03) and 77.3 mm over the table (layout 0), its fingers along +x toward the wrist. The hand turns on the finger rest's edge, 62 mm behind the ring's tip, and rests on the wrist rest by its weight: a press of 4.4 to 3.5 N on the fingertip's site tips it up unless the forearm stub (a 44 mm cylinder, 223 mm behind the ring's tip) is held down. The hand's base by seed (layout 0: shifted (0, 0) mm and turned 0 deg; layout 1: shifted (12, -10) mm and turned 6 deg; layout 2: shifted (-10, 12) mm and turned -6 deg).
scoring: The site: the pad of the middle or ring fingertip, 3 to 15 mm back from the apex and 15 to 45 deg round from the pad's middle line on either side; the shield's face within 1.5 mm of the skin is on it. Square: the lancet's axis within 15 deg of the skin's normal there. A slide: the face moving more than 1 mm on the skin between first touch (2 N) and firing; lifting off ends a placement. Steadied: the wrist rises at most 2 mm off its rest while the lancet presses on anything. Rungs at the last step: 0.2 the tab twisted off and the lancet out of the stand; 0.4 and pressed at 5 N or more square on the site, steadied; 0.6 and fired there, square, steadied, without a slide; 0.8 and the used lancet inside the sharps container, let go by both hands; 1.0 that held 1 s. Scored 0 from then on: the lancet lifted out with its tab on; a press with the hand not steadied; a slide; a fire off the site, on the little finger, or tilted; the lancet loose outside the stand and the container for 0.5 s (dropped); the hand's base dragged 5 mm; the lancet 30 mm under the table top; the firing model not running.
reset_notes: A new lancet in the socket each trial (a used one is spent, and its tab stays in the socket and is removed); the hand on its rests by seed; the container emptied of the trial's lancet.
fidelity: Approximate. The lancet's drive is a sprung shield that fires at a set force; the needle, the puncture and blood are not simulated. The tab is a sprung turn of its socket that counts as broken at 45 deg. The trainer hand is rigid on a pivot; skin does not deform. Lancet body sizes, the fire force within its source range and the tab torque are estimates, measured before real trials.
